column1: # The -Subject line each item type mark is generated from, so a regeneration
# matches, and a short note for the mark's own header.
# Written in the voice gluniverse-vtt's own subjects.tsv uses for the class
# sigils: a noun phrase describing what is in the picture, not a brief. The
# style paragraph in gen-type-marks.sh carries everything else, and it is the
# one the class sigils and the Artifice, Root and Void domain marks were drawn
# to — which is the whole point of this set existing. The thirteen hand-drawn
# geometric marks these replaced held at 14px but sat beside a domain plate
# One archetype each, so no two marks share a silhouette. Where count is the
# cue, it is the only difference: one spearhead against two, two lozenges

column2: two interlocking heraldic lozenges, one overlapping the other, the overlap cut out as a negative-space slit
column3: The lozenge is the heraldic charge for descent, and two of them joined is two lineages.

column2: three pointed shields clustered in a triangle, their edges almost meeting
column3: Three is the smallest count that reads as a group rather than a pair.

column2: a tall lozenge splitting open down its spine with a second lozenge turning out of it
column3: Ancestry is two lozenges side by side; this is one that became another.

column2: a war banner on a short staff, its foot cut into a deep swallow-tail
column3: The standard you fight under. Only ever drawn where a homebrew class names a domain of its own and the domain sigil cannot resolve.

column2: a heavy stem forking into two tapering arms, each ending in a hooked point
column3: A branch is the literal relation: a subclass is one of the ways a class goes. The same fallback as the class mark.

column2: a tall card with cut corners and a sharp lozenge pierced clean through its centre
column3: The card's own silhouette with its sigil voided. The rarest fallback of the three.

column2: a single broad spearhead, apex up, with swept shoulders and a short tang
column3: A point is the one weapon idea that is not also a genre.

column2: two slender spearheads side by side, points up, their shoulders swept outward
column3: The same idea twice, which is both the count cue and the literal answer: the secondary slot is where a second weapon goes.

column2: a segmented breastplate of three tapering bands, the lowest narrowest
column3: Not a shield — the rail already spends one on the Armor Score, and a second would claim the two are the same number.

column2: a stoppered flask with a faceted body and a narrow neck
column3: A vial, a canister and a cartridge all land on this silhouette.

column2: a buckled strap-plate with a lozenge boss at its centre
column3: The generic mark, so the generic shape: a thing you carry, without saying which thing.

column2: a strongbox with a heavy lid band and a lozenge latch
column3: Loot used to borrow the gear mark, and the two sit side by side on the gear tab.

column2: a broad upward chevron with barbed tapering tips
column3: The charge for something earned and held, which is what this catch-all subtype's members have in common.
